messages.subject: Re: Controlling opacity in bubble_plot
messages.body_plain:
I think you want colored points rather than bubbles for what you are
trying to do. The GUI does not allow you to set transparency on
points. You can do it in code though with something like:

data(LA_places)
plot.new <http://plot.new>()
par(mar=c(.5,.5,2.25,.5), oma=c(1,1,1,1))
plot.window(c(-1.3515289593271725E7,-1.2869549578318553E7),c(3787607.625475114,4260905.704606224),
xaxs = 'i', yaxs = 'i')
plot(openmap(c(35.71083783530009,-121.409912109375),c(32.18491105051798,-115.609130859375),7,'osm'),add=TRUE)

var <- LA_places@data[,'ID']
var <- round(100*(var+min(var))/max(var))
clrs <- heat.colors(100,alpha=.1) #set alpha here
var <- clrs[var]
x <- coordinates(LA_places)[,1]
y <- coordinates(LA_places)[,2]
points(x,y,col=var)
title('')

messages.subject: Spatial add-on -> changing background?
messages.body_plain:
Dear All,

I've just discovered Deducer (which is amazing) while looking for
spatial analysis techniques.

Is there any way to substitute the map background for a background of
one's choosing? In my particular case, an image of cells or tissue?

I realize this isn't what the spatial add-on was developed for and
perhaps there is other software which is more suitable, but the
spatial plotting is very nice. The possibility for combined spatial/
temporal analysis and plotting (stack of images) would be fantastic
(now I'm definitely asking too much).

Regardless, I will be using Deducer from now on. It is exactly what I
was looking for, thank you!

Kind regards,
Paul

messages.subject: What kind of kurtosis calculates Deducer?
messages.subject_clean: What kind of kurtosis calculates Deducer?
messages.body_plain: Kurtosis characterizes peakedness, where the normal distribution has a value of 3 and smaller values correspond to thinner tails (less peakedness). Some packages substract three (3) from the kurtosis, so that the normal distribution has a kurtosis of 0 (this is sometimes called "excess kurtosis". What kind of kurtosis calculates Deducer (menu Analysis>Descriptives)?

messages.subject_clean: What kind of kurtosis calculates Deducer?
messages.body_plain:
Deducer uses type two, the same as SAS/SPSS

G_2 = ((n+1) g_2 + 6) * (n-1) / ((n-2)(n-3))

ian
